say.description: What the action does, in plain words, as the policy card says it (for example "file a request").

level.description: The identity level the action needs: 0 anonymous, 1 the factors matched, 2 the factors and the one-time code (identity.yaml names them). Default 2, the highest, so an action left without one fails closed.

anyOf.description: A rule with no parameters: identity (R1, the caller's identity level is at least the action's) or attempts (R6, the identity check has failed fewer times than identity.yaml's attempts).

param.description: The action's param that is the subject's own id (for example accountId).

record.description: The action's param that is a record id the gate resolves to its owner (for example recordId).

scope.description: scope (R2): the subject the action acts on must be one the caller may see. Exactly one of "param" (the param is the subject's own id) or "record" (the param is a record id, resolved to its owner).

anyOf.description: The scope rule with its parameters, for example "scope: { param: accountId }".

reason.description: The reason a "person" role hands the call over for (its handoff line is handoff_<reason>). Default "role-person".

role.description: role (R5): what each role may do with the action: allow, refuse, or person (a person takes the call). A role not listed is refused, and so is a party who acts for subjects with no role; one of the app's subjects passes. The roles are those identity.yaml declares under principals.

anyOf.description: The role rule with its parameters, for example "role: { viewer: refuse, clerk: person }".

confirmed.description: confirmed (R3): the action sends exactly these fields, and the caller confirmed exactly these values at the read-back, in the order the hash is taken over.

anyOf.description: The confirmed rule with its parameters, for example "confirmed: [accountId, note]".

fields.description: fields (R7): the only fields the action may send on (to a downstream service). An empty list sends none.

anyOf.description: The fields rule with its parameters, for example "fields: [note, date]".

field.description: The action's param that holds the date (yyyy-mm-dd). A value that is not a date BLOCKs.

notBefore.description: The earliest date the value may be, inclusive: "today", a date, or a reference to a lookup that gives one.

notAfter.description: The latest date the value may be, inclusive: "today", a date, or a reference to a lookup that gives one.

within.description: A reference to a lookup that gives a window, { start, end } (end null: open-ended), the value must be inside, ends inclusive. A lookup that gives null has no window: the value is outside it.

reasons.description: The reason the gate gives for each way the rule fails, for the app's refusal lines and handoffs.

invalid.description: The reason a value that is not a date is refused for. Default "not-a-date".

outOfRange.description: The reason a date before notBefore or after notAfter fails for. Default "date-range".

outsideWindow.description: The reason a date outside the window fails for. Default "date-window".

verdicts.description: The verdict for a date out of its bounds or outside its window. A value that is not a date, and a bound that cannot be found, always BLOCK.

outOfRange.description: BLOCK (default) or NEEDS_HUMAN, for a date out of its bounds.

outsideWindow.description: BLOCK (default) or NEEDS_HUMAN, for a date outside the window.

dateInRange.description: dateInRange: the action's date param is a date within its bounds, each inclusive. At least one of notBefore, notAfter, within.

anyOf.description: The dateInRange rule with its parameters, for example "dateInRange: { field: returnDate, notAfter: today }".

field.description: The action's param that holds the number: digits, an optional leading minus and an optional point with digits; no units, separators or spaces. Anything else BLOCKs.

min.description: The smallest the number may be, inclusive: a number, or a reference to a lookup that gives one.

max.description: The largest the number may be, inclusive: a number, or a reference to a lookup that gives one (for example orderTotal(orderId), or order(orderId).total).

reasons.description: The reason the gate gives for each way the rule fails.

invalid.description: The reason a value that is not a number is refused for. Default "not-a-number".

outOfRange.description: The reason a number below min or above max fails for. Default "limit".

verdicts.description: The verdict for a number outside its limits. A value that is not a number, and a bound that cannot be found, always BLOCK.

outOfRange.description: BLOCK (default) or NEEDS_HUMAN, for a number outside its limits.

limit.description: limit: the action's number param is within its limits, each inclusive. At least one of min, max.

anyOf.description: The limit rule with its parameters, for example "limit: { field: amount, max: orderTotal(orderId) }".

custom.description: custom: one of the app's own rules, by the id its code registers it under (code.customRules).

anyOf.description: The custom rule with its parameters, for example "custom: <the rule's id in code.customRules>".

items.description: One rule: a bare name (identity, attempts) or a map of one rule to its parameters (scope, role, confirmed, fields, dateInRange, limit, custom).

rules.description: The rules the gate runs before the action, in this order; the first that fails decides. An empty list runs none.

additionalProperties.description: One action: what it is, the identity level it needs and the rules the gate runs before it.

actions.description: Every action the agent may take, by tool name, with the level it needs and the rules the gate runs before it. Every tool of the app needs an entry; anything not listed is refused.

purposes.description: The identity level each purpose needs (what a caller wants done, a form id, before any tool is called), when it is more than its first action's. Default: none.

level.description: The identity level the purpose needs.

additionalProperties.description: One purpose and the level it needs.

scope.description: The scope rule's (R2) description, by who asks and how the action names its subject. Default: "The record belongs to someone this caller may see".

subject.description: The scope rule's description when one of the app's subjects asks.

record.description: The scope rule's description when the action names its subject by a record id the gate resolves to its owner.

param.description: The scope rule's description when the action names its subject by the subject's own id.

delegate.description: The scope rule's description when a party acting for subjects asks.

record.description: The scope rule's description when the action names its subject by a record id the gate resolves to its owner.

param.description: The scope rule's description when the action names its subject by the subject's own id.

recordOwner.description: What the scope rule's compared line calls the owner of a record. Default "record owner".

subject.description: What the scope rule's compared line calls a subject named by id. Default "subject".

role.description: The role rule's (R5) compared line, by what the rule gives the role, as a template with {role} and {tool}.

allow.description: The role rule's compared line when the role may take the action. Write {role} and {tool} where they go. Default "role {role} may {tool}: yes".

refuse.description: The role rule's compared line when the role is refused the action. Default "role {role} may {tool}: no".

person.description: The role rule's compared line when a person takes the call. Default "role {role} may {tool}: with a person".

wording.description: The words the gate's built-in rules use in their description and compared lines, so the console and the audit read in the app's terms. Without it, neutral words.

additionalProperties.description: The fields of the action's result withheld (set to null) from this party. Each must be one the tool declares (its fields, in code). An empty list withholds nothing, so a role can see what its kind may not.
The actions whose results are redacted for this party, each with the fields withheld.

redact.description: What a party who acts for subjects does not get to see of what an action returns, by delegate kind (agent) or by kind and role (agent.clerk), whose list for an action replaces the kind's. The tool returns the whole record and the engine strips the fields before any hook, line, trace, console or audit sees it. A subject acting for themselves is never redacted. Default: nothing is withheld.

description: policy.yaml: what the agent may do, action by action. Custom rule functions stay in code; this file names them.
